questions.question: How do you stop a skid caused by pressing the accelerator too hard?

options.text: Press the accelerator harder.
Take your foot off the accelerator.
Stop the vehicle completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Skids from acceleration happen on slippery roads. You can stop them by taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.question: What is true about hydroplaning?

options.text: It rarely happens to trucks.
It usually happens above 65 mph.
It can happen with just a little water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a little water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip and slide on water. You do not need a lot of water for this to happen. It can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: What are signs of drowsy driving?

options.text: Your eyes go out of focus by themselves.
You have trouble holding your head up.
You drift from lane to lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsy driving include eyes closing or losing focus, trouble keeping your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They can replace flat mirrors.
They help you see a wider area.
They are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved mirrors used on large vehicles. They let you see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Is the posted design speed for a curve always safe for buses?

options.text: Yes, it is safe for buses.
Yes, it is safe for all vehicles, including buses.
No, it is the minimum speed required.
No, it is not always safe for buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is not always safe for buses.
questions.explanation: A bus can roll over or slide off the road even when driven at the posted speed for a curve in good weather. For safety, slow down before driving a bus around a curve.

questions.question: Which vehicles have the most trouble with strong winds?

options.text: Lighter vehicles.
Heavier vehicles.
Flatbed trailers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavier vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. This is especially true for drivers of lighter commercial vehicles.

questions.question: Is driving at night safer than driving during the day?

options.text: Yes, it is safer.
It is just as safe.
No, it is more dangerous.
It is discouraged.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see hazards, headlight glare affects vision, and there are more tired and impaired drivers on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver?

options.text: Follow closely behind them.
Flash your lights at them.
Stay far away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from them.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space and keep a safe distance behind them.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up?

options.text: Go as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Walk your path first to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk your path first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk along the path to look for obstacles. Back up slowly and use both side mirrors to check.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel, what should you check?

options.text: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and locking jaws.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the fifth wheel, look in the gap and make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: When starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, the driver should:

options.text: Listen for unusual noises.
Rev the engine.
Turn up the radio.
Turn on the heater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, listen for any unusual noises. This is part of checking your engine during the pre-trip inspection.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Not light up or sound at all.
Turn on and then shut off quickly.
Turn on and stay on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on and then shut off quickly.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn on briefly and then turn off quickly.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be required to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Walk around the vehicle.
Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.
Crawl under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crawl under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each item, and explain what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the vehicle or hood.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop your vehicle within:

options.text: 10 feet of your vehicle.
1,000 feet of your vehicle.
Your line of sight ahead on the road.
30 seconds of hitting the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your line of sight ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop your vehicle within the distance you can see ahead on the road. Slow down whenever visibility is reduced.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people not paying attention to the road. Watch out for road workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road. A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus is not a safety concern.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirrors.
Use both side mirrors.
Only use the passenger's side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors frequently while backing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of hydraulic brake failure?

options.text: Loss of hydraulic pressure
Brake fade from overuse on long hills
Downshifting

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens due to loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade from overuse on long hills. Downshifting does not cause hydraulic brake failure.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Signal before the turn.
Turn off your signal just before starting the turn.
Signal only if vehicles are in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before the turn.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal well before making a turn or changing lanes. Keep the signal on during the turn. Turn it off after the turn is complete, unless your vehicle has self-canceling signals.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem with your vehicle while driving, you should:

options.text: Ignore it and see if it goes away.
Write a report that describes the problem.
Try to fix it yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report that describes the problem.
questions.explanation: At the end of each driving day, you may need to write a report about the vehicle. Note any issues that could affect safety or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, a driver should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the left. Park completely within the space boundaries.
